name: Jaldapara Tourist Lodge (WBTDC)
price_band: Government mid-range rates; check the current WBTDC tariff (indicative)
summary: The West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's lodge at Madarihat, a short drive from the Jaldapara park gate and the safari counters. Plain, reliable and the easiest base for an early jeep safari without a long dark drive.
body: Madarihat is the small highway town at the western edge of Jaldapara National Park, and this is the state tourism corporation's lodge there. Expect a government-lodge feel: big rooms, a dining hall with a fixed Bengali and North Indian menu, a garden, and staff who know the safari routine because most guests come for the same reason. Rooms are booked through WBTDC, not through the forest department.

We suggest it for families and first-timers who want a known name and a short morning run to the park. It is not inside the forest, so you will not hear rhinos at night. Book well ahead for October to March weekends and the Puja holidays, and check current status before you travel: the October 2025 floods damaged roads and bridges around Jaldapara.
why: Minutes from the Madarihat safari counters, so dawn shifts are easy
Government rates and a predictable standard
Food on site, which matters in a small town after dark

faqs.q: How do I book the Jaldapara Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Book through the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation, either on its official website or at a WBTDC office in Kolkata or Siliguri. Rooms are released in advance and fill early for October to March weekends and the Puja holidays. Safari seats are a separate booking with the forest department, so do not assume the lodge can arrange them.

faqs.q: Is the Jaldapara Tourist Lodge the same as Hollong?
faqs.a: No. This lodge is at Madarihat, on the highway outside the park. Hollong was the old wooden forest bungalow deep inside Jaldapara, which was gutted by fire in June 2024. Check current status before you travel if you read about Hollong reopening, because older blog posts still describe it as running.

faqs.q: Can I walk to the safari gate from the lodge?
faqs.a: The forest office and safari counters are a short drive away, and most guests use a hired jeep or the safari jeep itself. Walking along the highway in the dark before a 6 am shift is not a good idea, because elephants cross roads around Madarihat. Ask the lodge desk to fix a car the evening before.

name: Murti Banani Eco-Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
price_band: ₹1,800–4,000 a room, tent from about ₹1,500 (indicative, WBFDC tariff)
summary: The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's cottages beside the Murti river at Uttar Dhupjhora, between Gorumara and Chapramari. Room categories from standard to premium, plus tents, and a riverbank that most guests never want to leave.
body: Banani has been the default Murti stay for Bengali families for a long time. Cottages sit in a wooded compound a short walk from the Murti riverbed, which is wide, stony and shallow for most of the dry season. The corporation lists several room grades and tents, a local menu, and an evening folk dance on some nights; ask what is running when you book.

It suits people who want a forest-edge base for both Gorumara and Chapramari safaris without the roadside resort strip of Lataguri. Food is charged separately on most plans. Book on the WBFDC website, and check current status before you travel, since the corporation revises tariffs and closes some properties for repairs after the monsoon.
why: On the Murti river, between two parks
Government tariff with several price levels, including tents
Quieter than the highway resorts of Lataguri

faqs.q: How far is Murti Banani from the Gorumara safari counters?
faqs.a: Murti is roughly 10–15 km from Lataguri, where the Gorumara watchtower tickets are usually sold, about 20–30 minutes by car. Chapramari is a similar distance in the other direction. Fix your safari slot first and then arrange a car or the safari jeep pickup with the counter or your driver.

faqs.q: Can we swim in the Murti river?
faqs.a: Paddling at the edge in winter is common, but the river rises fast after rain in the hills upstream, even when it is dry at Murti. Do not swim in the main channel, keep children within reach and leave the riverbed at once if the water turns brown or the level starts to climb.

faqs.q: Are meals included at Murti Banani?
faqs.a: Not on most plans. The corporation lists food as a separate charge, and recent tariffs have been about ₹500 per person a day at its smaller camps. Ask for the current meal plan when booking. There are a few small eateries near Murti bridge, but choice after dark is thin.

name: Dhupjhora Elephant Camp (WBFDC)
price_band: About ₹2,000 a cottage plus meals (indicative, WBFDC tariff)
summary: A small forest corporation camp at Dakshin Dhupjhora on the edge of Gorumara, with a handful of cottages, including raised tree-house style rooms. The forest department's trained elephants are kept nearby, and mornings start with their bath in the river.
body: Dhupjhora is one of the community-linked eco camps the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation runs around Gorumara, alongside Kalipur, Ramsai and Murti. It is small, with only a few cottages, so it books out early. The draw is the forest department's working elephants, the kunkis used for patrols, and the chance to watch them being bathed and fed.

Facilities are simple and meals, local performances and an attendant are charged separately on the corporation's tariff. This is a place for people who want to hear the forest at night, not for room service. Elephant rides for visitors run only when the department allows them: check current status before you travel.
why: One of the few stays right on the forest edge
Forest department elephants next door
Government tariff, small and quiet

faqs.q: Can we ride the elephants at Dhupjhora?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Elephant rides for visitors in Gorumara have been offered from Dhupjhora and other camps in some seasons and suspended in others. Watching the morning bath is the dependable part. Ask the corporation or the forest office when you book, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do we reach Dhupjhora?
faqs.a: Dhupjhora is near Murti, roughly 15 km from Lataguri and about 75–80 km from Siliguri by road via Malbazar. Most guests come by reserved car from NJP or Bagdogra, about ₹3,000–4,000. Bus travellers can get off at Lataguri or Batabari and take a local car for the last stretch.

faqs.q: Is it safe to stay so close to the forest?
faqs.a: Yes, if you follow camp rules. Wild elephants and gaur do move near the camps, especially at dusk. Stay inside the compound after dark, use a torch, do not walk to the river at night and never approach elephants for photographs, including the camp's own animals without their mahouts.

name: Lataguri Eco-Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
summary: The forest corporation's own property at Lataguri, the village on the Gorumara forest edge where the safari tickets are sold. A government alternative to the long line of private resorts on the highway, with the park counters a few minutes away.
body: Lataguri grew from a forest-edge village into the main resort strip for Gorumara, with dozens of private hotels on and off the highway. The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's eco-tourism centre here gives you a government-run option close to the safari counters, so you can be in the queue early without a drive.

Room categories and tariffs change, so check the corporation's site when you plan. Ask whether meals are included, and ask for a room away from the highway side if you are a light sleeper, because trucks run through Lataguri at night. Check current status before you travel.
why: Walkable to the Gorumara safari counter area
Government-run, with published tariffs
A good base for Lataguri, Medla and Chukchuki slots

faqs.q: Does staying at the Lataguri Eco-Tourism Centre include a safari?
faqs.a: No. Safari and watchtower slots are booked separately with the forest department, online or at the counter, and a jeep is hired on top. Staying close to the counters helps if you are trying for a same-day slot, which is possible on weekdays and hard on weekends and holidays.

faqs.q: How far is Lataguri from NJP station?
faqs.a: About 75–85 km, two to two and a half hours by car via Sevoke, Odlabari and Malbazar, or via Jalpaiguri and Maynaguri. A reserved car costs about ₹3,000–3,500. Buses towards Malbazar and Maynaguri are far cheaper, about ₹100–150, but slower.

faqs.q: Is Lataguri noisy?
faqs.a: The village sits on a busy highway through the forest, and speed limits apply but trucks run at night. Rooms set back from the road are quieter. If silence matters more than convenience, look at Murti or the corporation's smaller camps such as Dhupjhora and Kalipur instead.

name: Suntaleykhola Eco-Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
price_band: ₹2,500–3,000 a cottage, tent about ₹1,500 (indicative, WBFDC tariff)
summary: Forest corporation cottages beside the Suntalekhola stream, about 5 km beyond Samsing on the edge of Neora Valley National Park. Reached across a hanging footbridge, which is half the fun and the reason to pack light.
body: Suntalekhola, the orange stream in Nepali, runs out of the Neora Valley forest into the Murti. The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's cottages sit on the far bank, and the last few minutes are on foot over a suspension bridge above the water. The corporation also runs a separate river camp nearby with tents.

Expect simple cottages, home-style food and a lot of birdsong. There is no market here; Samsing is the nearest place for shops. Mobile signal is patchy. Book on the corporation's website and check current status before you travel, because the road above Samsing is narrow and monsoon damage is common.
why: Riverside cottages reached by a footbridge
On the edge of Neora Valley National Park
Cheaper than most private resorts in Samsing

faqs.q: Can a car reach the Suntaleykhola cottages?
faqs.a: A car reaches the road end near the bridge, and you walk the last short stretch over the suspension bridge with your bags. Pack in one soft bag if you can. People with limited mobility should ask the corporation about the walk before booking, because there are steps and an uneven path.

faqs.q: How far is Suntalekhola from Siliguri?
faqs.a: Roughly 90 km, about three hours by car via Malbazar, Chalsa, Metali and Samsing. A reserved car costs about ₹3,500–4,500 one way from NJP. Shared jeeps and buses reach Chalsa or Metali, where local jeeps run up to Samsing on a less regular timetable.

faqs.q: Is Suntalekhola open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The forest corporation's property is not inside a national park, so it may stay open, but the road above Samsing and the stream itself can be risky in heavy rain. We do not recommend June to September. If you go, keep a free day for road closures and check current status before you travel.

name: Jholung River Camp (WBFDC)
summary: The forest corporation's camp at Jhalong on the Jaldhaka river, close to the Bhutan border. A base for river birding, the drive up to Paren and the last road to Bindu, at a fraction of what a private resort charges.
body: Jhalong (the corporation spells it Jholung) is a small settlement built around the Jaldhaka hydel project, with the river running wide and cold below the road. The corporation's river camp offers cottages in a few grades within sight and sound of the water. It is a place to sit by the river with tea and a pair of binoculars.

There are only a few tea shops and small stores in Jhalong, so take snacks and cash. Mobile signal varies by network. Book through the corporation's website and check current status before you travel, because the hill road from Chalsa and the Jaldhaka valley are prone to slides and flood damage in the monsoon.
why: On the Jaldhaka, a good river-bird stretch
Close to Bindu and Paren
Government tariff in a valley with few stays

faqs.q: How do we get to Jhalong?
faqs.a: Jhalong is about 100 km from Siliguri, three to three and a half hours by car via Malbazar and Chalsa, then up the Jaldhaka valley road. A reserved car from NJP costs about ₹4,000–5,000. Local jeeps run from Chalsa and nearby markets, but timings are irregular and fewer after noon.

faqs.q: Can we see Bhutan from Jhalong?
faqs.a: The Jaldhaka forms the border with Bhutan a little further up at Bindu, and the hills across the river there are Bhutanese territory. There is no official crossing for visitors at Jhalong or Bindu. Indian travellers enter Bhutan at Phuentsholing, opposite Jaigaon, with the paperwork Bhutan requires.

faqs.q: Is Jhalong good for birdwatching?
faqs.a: Yes. The river and forested banks hold river birds such as forktails, redstarts and wagtails in winter, along with forest species on the slopes. Go out at first light, walk the road along the river, and keep to the bank, away from the hydel installations, where photography may be restricted.

name: Mendabari Jungle Lodge (WBFDC)
summary: A small forest corporation lodge in the Dakshin Barajhar forest at Mendabari, in the Chilapata belt between Jaldapara and Buxa. The British called the Nalraja Garh ruins nearby the Mendabari ruins, and the lodge is your closest bed to them.
body: Mendabari is a forest village on the Chilapata side of Jaldapara, close to the Hasimara–Kodalbasti road. The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's lodge here has only a few rooms, so it is quiet and fills fast in winter. Rhinos and elephants use this forest, and staff will tell you plainly to stay inside the compound after dark.

It works well for a night between Jaldapara and Buxa, with a Chilapata jeep safari and the walk around the Nalraja Garh ruins. Food is simple and should be ordered in advance. Book through the corporation's website, and check current status before you travel, because the October 2025 floods hit this river belt hard.
why: Inside the Chilapata forest belt
Close to the Nalraja Garh ruins
Small and quiet, at a government tariff

faqs.q: How far is Mendabari from Hasimara station?
faqs.a: Roughly 10–15 km, about half an hour by car through forest. Hasimara is on the Dooars railway line between Siliguri and Alipurduar, and trains from NJP or Siliguri Junction take about four to five hours. Arrange a car through the lodge or at Hasimara; there is no regular public transport into Mendabari.

faqs.q: Can we visit Nalraja Garh from Mendabari?
faqs.a: Yes. The ruins are inside the Chilapata forest and visits are made on the forest department's jeep safari, not on foot alone. A six-seat jeep with entry and guide costs roughly ₹2,500–3,500 (indicative 2025–26). Check current status before you travel, since routes can close after flood damage.

faqs.q: Is there a market or ATM near Mendabari?
faqs.a: No. Hasimara and Madarihat have shops, eateries and ATMs. Carry enough cash for the safari, meals and tips before you drive into the forest, since card payments and UPI work only where the signal holds, which is not everywhere in Chilapata.
